title: Post-hoc smooth thermal aliases and invalid acceleration calibration
status: Post-hoc adversarial diagnostic after the spectral-response development benchmark. No frozen benchmark threshold or original inference result is changed. Established aliasing is the mechanism; no novelty claim.
family: A_q=A_base tensor I_2 + I_2 tensor [[0,-b],[b,0]], A_base=[[0,-sqrt(kappa)],[sqrt(kappa),-nu]], b=2*pi*q/Delta. Observed velocity is first coordinate, equilibrium covariance I_4, diffusion Q=diag(0,0,2nu,2nu).
input: results/spectral_response/input_scatter_matrices.npz; all 12 saved velocity datasets at M=4096 have the same sampling law under every alias.
invalid_calibration: Independent pairs of velocities separated by Delta produce finite differences (v(Delta)-v(0))/Delta, variance 2*(1-C_base(Delta))/Delta^2. A valid chi-square upper limit for this finite-difference variance is deliberately MISUSED as an instantaneous acceleration-variance upper bound. Returned intervals are invalid for the aliased truth; their failed inclusion is the diagnostic.
valid_control: Recompute with the alias's exact instantaneous acceleration variance kappa+b^2 supplied as labeled oracle information. No hardware calibration is simulated for this control.
checks: Full and hidden drift stability; Gibbs Lyapunov identity; generalized time reversal; covariance product identity; all observed lags equal; acceleration variance; finite-difference variance; positive-real memory screen; DC diffusivity identity; integrated displacement versus direct oscillatory quadrature; source-input provenance; valid-oracle bound control.
scope: Both families are free-position, stable, passive thermal velocity models with finite acceleration variance. Free position itself has no normalizable equilibrium distribution. Ideal instantaneous acceleration and finite differences are distinct observables. No claim that all experimental acceleration measurements fail.
